title.narrative: Integrated Urban Environmental Management in the Tonle Sap Basin Project

description.narrative: The project will finance environmental infrastructure (for flood protection, drainage, wastewater management and treatment, and solid waste management) in Kampong Chhnang and Pursat. The project will finance small-scale community-driven environmental infrastructure; strengthen sector operations and coordination; and build capacity for project management and operations and maintenance.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Improved urban services and enhanced climate change resilience in participating municipalities

At least 31,500 people consistently using safe sanitation services (at least 15,000 women) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: A total of 62,600 people (design population in 2040) are expected to benefit from the improved sanitation services as shown below. Pursat Municipality: 20,000 persons. Kampong Chhnang Municipality: 42,600 persons Data Source: Annual reports and project performance monitoring reports by PIUs and MPWT, ADB loan missions, and PCR

At least 76,500 people consistently using safe solid waste management services Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: At least 181,077 persons (projected population for 2030) in both KC and Pursat Municipalities will have access to safe solid waste management services. Kampong Chhnang: 71,611 persons = (15,914 HHs) Pursat: 109,466 persons = (21,893 HHs). Construction of the project's landfills were completed on 27 May 2022 and handed over to the local authorities on 24 February 2023. Kampong Chhnang started operations on 17 February 2024 and Pursat landfill started operations on 17 April 2024 Data Source: Annual reports and project performance monitoring reports by PIUs and MPWT, ADB loan missions, and PCR

100,000 residents of the project municipal government areas benefit from the project Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Total population of both cities is approx. 114,379. -Population in Kampong Chhnang town: 42,335 - Population in Pursat town: 72,062 Data Source: Annual reports and project performance monitoring reports by PIUs and MPWT, ADB loan missions, and PCR Baseline value: n/a

At least 3,000 households benefit from reduced flooding through improved drainage Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: A total of 4,193 households (20,965 people) from both towns are expected to benefit from reduced flooding due to the drainage improvements. In Kampong Chhnang 1,179 HHs (approx. 5,895 people) and in Pursat 3,014 HHs (approx. 15,070 people). Data Source: Annual reports and project performance monitoring reports by PIUs and MPWT, ADB loan missions, and PCR Baseline value: n/a

Sanitation and solid waste management units are funded as per the agreed budgets from the provincial governments Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Government to formally issue its decision on the entities who will manage the project assets. Discussions are ongoing between ADB and the EA. And the EA and other government units to address this matter. Data Source: Provincial and municipal financial statements and payroll information, provincial government budget commitment letters Base year: 2020 Baseline value: N
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Urban infrastructure improved Indicator: 30 km sewers inclusive of main and collection pipelines and household connections. Progress/Status: 12.28 km of main sewer and 19.54 km of sewage collector lines networks and 500 household connections Data Source: Annual reports and project performance monitoring reports by PIUs and MPWT, ADB loan missions, and PCR Actual value:

Output: Urban infrastructure improved Indicator: 87 km of stormwater drains newly rehabilitated and constructed Progress/Status: A combined total of 72.73 km of drains have been rehabilitated and constructed. In Pursat: 25.54 km of new drains were constructed; 27.19 km of existing drains were rehabilitated and cleaned. Total for Pursat = 52.73 km Construction works were completed on 19 June 2023. In Kampong Chhnang: 8.0 km of new drainage lines were installed; 12.0 km of existing drainage lines were cleaned and rehabilitated. Total for Kampong Chhnang = 20.00 km Data Source: Annual reports and project performance monitoring reports by PIUs and MPWT, ADB loan missions, and PCR Actual value:

Output: Urban infrastructure improved Indicator: Two controlled landfills with a capacity of 60,000 tonnes of municipal waste constructed and operational Progress/Status: Total for the controlled landfill in both towns = 156,000 tons. Kampong Chhnang landfill capacity: 72,000 tons Pursat landfill capacity:84,000 tons All works for the landfills have been completed. Equipment to operate the landfills was delivered to the local authorities in Kampong Chhnang and Pursat on 14 & 15 December 2023 respectively. Kampong Chhnang started operations on 17 February 2024. Pursat landfill started operations on 17 April 2024. O&M training for both landfills has been conducted.
Data Source: Annual reports and project performance monitoring reports by PIUs and MPWT, ADB loan missions, and PCR Actual value:

Output: Urban infrastructure improved Indicator: Two wastewater treatment plants with capacity of at least 6 MLD constructed and made operational Progress/Status: Two WWTPs with a total capacity of 7.3 MLD has been constructed as explained below: Pursat sewerage collection system and WWTP (capacity = 2.1 MLD) works were completed on 19 June 2023. Construction of Kampong Chhnang WWTP (capacity = 5.2 MLD) commenced on 1st February 2023, and completed in January 2025. O&M training for both WWTPs has been conducted Data Source: Annual reports and project performance monitoring reports by PIUs and MPWT, ADB loan missions, and PCR Actual value:

Output: Urban infrastructure improved Indicator: At least 5,400 ID Poor 1 & 2 and vulnerable households (20% female headed) have pour-flush toilets Progress/Status: A total of 1,447 latrines (740 for ID Poor & 707 for vulnerable groups) were constructed. In Pursat 154 latrines for ID Poor (77 = 50% FHHs households) only, no vulnerable groups. In Kampong Chhnang, 1,293 latrines were constructed, including 702 (54%) for female-headed households. This total includes 586 ID Poor latrines and 707 latrines for vulnerable groups identified by the Provincial Authority in conjunction with the village chiefs. Data Source: Annual reports and project performance monitoring reports by PIUs and MPWT, ADB loan missions, and PCR Actual value:

Output: Institutional effectiveness improved Indicator: Capacity development program adopted for sanitation and solid waste management units in the participating municipalities, with at least 50 staff trained (30% women) Progress/Status: O&M trainings have been conducted for both towns. The number of staff trained is shown below. Sanitation: - Pursat: 18 (8=44% female) participants, - Kampong Chhnang: 22 (10=45% female) participants - Total 40 (18=45% females) participants, Solid waste: - Pursat: 61 (17=28% female) participants, - Kampong Chhnang: 66 (15=23% female) participants - Total 127 (32=25% females) participants Grand-total for all trainings: - Sanitation: 40 (18=45% female) participants - Solid Waste: 127 (32=25% female) participants Grand-Total: 167 (50=30% female) participants Data Source: Annual reports and project performance monitoring reports by PIUs and MPWT, ADB loan missions, PMC, NGO and PCR. Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y

Output: Institutional effectiveness improved Indicator: Gender-sensitive hygiene promotion campaigns conducted in each participating municipality with women accounting for at least 40% of participants Progress/Status: Gender sensitive hygiene promotion campaign was successfully conducted in both provinces. The total number of participants attending the campaigndirect beneficiaries') included: - Pursat: 192 (137=71% female) participants, - Kampong Chhnang: 117 (74=63% female) participants - Total 309 (211=68% females) participants, Prior to the promotion campaign 60 (39=65% females) participants from both towns: KCG=30 (19=63%females) and PRS=30 (20=67%females) attended the campaign trainings. Data Source: Annual reports and project performance monitoring reports by PIUs and MPWT, ADB loan missions, PMC, NGO and PCR. Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y

Output: Institutional effectiveness improved Indicator: Sanitation and waste management units established in the participating municipalities and become operational (20% of staff are women) Progress/Status: The USUs for the solid waste management for both Kampong Chhnang and Pursat Provinces have been established under the Provincial Authorities. Sewerage and Wastewater Treatment Plant Management units, under DPWT for each town, are being established. MPWT is processing the relevant documentation. To ensure 20% of staff within the units are female, a mandate requiring 20% female staff is recruited has been included in the Operations and Maintenance (O&M) manual. Data Source: Official Provincial decisions confirming the establishment and staffing details of the sanitation and solid waste management units. Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y

Output: Policy and regulatory environment improved Indicator: Climate resilient recommendations and gender-responsive and inclusive climate adaptation action plan developed Progress/Status: The report on Climate Change Adaptation in Urban Development was presented in June 2018. Review and update was made in March 2025. Data Source: Report and attendance records of national workshop to present proposals Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y

Output: Policy and regulatory environment improved Indicator: Recommendations on wastewater treatment standards and sludge disposal regulations (Baseline: Subdecree 27 [1999] and Subdecree 235 [2017]) Progress/Status: (i)Sub-Degree 103 of 29 June 2021 on wastewater treatment standard was issued. (ii) MPWT's Prakas 038 on 11 March 2023 on adoption of National Guideline on Fecal Sludge treatment standard using planted Drying Beds Technology. (iii) MPWT's Prakas 040 on adoption of Technical Specification for sewerage works. (iv) The sewerage law was promulgated on 22 November 2024.
Data Source: Recommended wastewater and sludge management standards submitted to MoE by MPWT and draft sanitation law Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y
